order: Apply a second class-boundary redraw scoped strictly to the three findings in the prior disagreement ledger. Recast one discriminator on where the evidence lives: evidence existing solely during a live run routes one way, while evidence persisting in a readable artifact routes the other, and a symptom merely being active or recurring never by itself counts as a running requirement; mirror that wording in the phase-chain rule and the related discriminator. Add a new discriminator closing the gap between the two ambiguous classes, keyed on whether content was recovered by reconciling a corpus or settled at intake. Give one discriminator an explicit unit definition, where an acceptance unit must span two or more components, and add a preamble rule scoping each discriminator strictly to its own two classes. Resolve the three flagged items and log any agreed item that shifts under the tightened rule. Leave validation of this redraw an open decision for the owner before the work order proceeds.
claims: All three flagged items resolved determinately under the redrawn boundary — one to a running class, one to a settled class, one to an evidence class — and one previously agreed item was found to shift under the tightened unit rule and was logged openly rather than silently changed. No class pair reached the three-entry merge trigger; the two closest pairs stand at exactly two each. The redraw was narrowly scoped, and validating it was left an open decision for the owner.
